title: What if Earth's air had 35% oxygen? 🔥
subject: oxygen
description:
Would you want to live on that planet? 👇

What would happen if Earth's atmosphere had 35% oxygen instead of 21%? Fossil charcoal shows fires get far easier above 25%, and about 300 million years ago giant griffinflies flew in oxygen-rich air.

Sources: Glasspool & Scott 2010, Nature Geoscience (Field Museum / Royal Holloway, "Oxygen fuels the fires of time"); Clapham & Karr 2012, PNAS (UC Santa Cruz, "Reign of the giant insects ended with the evolution of birds")
tags: what if earth had more oxygen
too much oxygen in the air

scenes.text: At 35% oxygen, even soaking-wet rainforests would burn.
You breathe 21% today. Ian Glasspool of Chicago's Field Museum found that above 25%, wet plants can catch fire.
At 30 to 35%, wildfires turn frequent and catastrophic.
Earth has been there. About 300 million years ago, oxygen topped 30%, and griffinflies flew on 70-centimeter wings.
Scientists think richer air let insects, which breathe through tiny tubes, grow far bigger.
On that planet, one lightning bolt could ignite a rain-soaked forest.
